In developing countries, genotype 1 and 2 are most prevalent, the virus is transmitted primarily through contaminated water and mostly cause epidemics of acute self-limiting viral hepatitis. In developed countries, genotype 3 is predominantly transmitted primarily through contaminated food, such as undercooked meat. This can cause chronic hepatitis in immunocompromised patients and can progress to cirrhosis within three to five years, which is much far more aggressive than what is seen with hepatitis C or hepatitis B. With no approved therapies for HEV, there is a significant unmet need for treatment options. Moving to slide 19.
